newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares close lower in apathetic trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares close lower in apathetic trade.

text.p: Lima shares fell slightly Monday, due mostly to the absence of foreign investors who await a key presidential speech July 28, in the hope it would clear the way following the country's recent political problems.
Analysts predicted the same trend Tuesday, but noted interest in mining companies benefiting from the ongoing rise in zinc prices, and the construction sector.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index dropped 0.93 percent to 2,097.35 points, while the blue-chip selective index fell 1.76 percent to 2,958.85 points.
The total amount traded was 27.1 million soles ($10 million) in 1,713 transactions.

"Investors are waiting for the address of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori during the national independence celebrations, because they believe he will give an outline of the politics of his government," said analyst Luis Cueva from Argos brokerage. "They also hope that he will resolve the recent allegations against the government."

He was referring to, among other things, President Alberto Fujimori's reshuffle of the cabinet Thursday, allegations of phone tapping by the secret services, the revocation of local citizenship from Israeli-born TV station owner Baruch Ivcher and a mass demonstration Thursday at the presidential palace.
The market Monday was also cautiously waiting for U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, to present Congress with a report on the state of the U.S. economy Tuesday.
"We will see what Greenspan says on the evolution of the U.S. economy, and I don't believe it will be anything bad," said an analyst from Lider brokerage.
Declining stocks today included miner Morococha which fell 6.54 percent to 7.15 soles and brewer Union de Cervecerias Backus y Johnston down 1.72 percent to 2.28 soles.

The share value of Morococha has suffered since it failed in the bid for the Mahr Tunel mining unit Friday. The winner of the sale, Volcan, saw its share value rocket 10.01 percent to 8.80 soles Monday.
Other winners included miner Perubar with 10 percent to 8.80 soles and cement-producer Cementos Lima with 0.17 percent to 5.81 soles.
Market leader Telefonica del Peru remained stable at 6.20 soles.
